newsitem.title: USA: WorldCom stock robust after upbeat meeting.
newsitem.headline: WorldCom stock robust after upbeat meeting.

text.p: WorldCom Inc was the most actively traded stock on the Nasdaq stock market Tuesday following an upbeat meeting by the company's senior management with analysts the previous day.

Shares of the diversified communications provider closed up 1-1/8 at 31 on volume of 11.3 million shares, after an all day Monday meeting which Merrill Lynch analyst Mark Kastan said highlighted WorldCom's strong strategic positioning.
Linda Meltzer, analyst at UBS Securities, said: "Yesterday was a very solid display by management of (their) story. It probably whet appetites of those who didn't own the stock."
In the meeting, management reaffirmed confidence in the consensus earnings estimate of $0.36 per share for 1997 and $0.80 per share in 1998, Kastan said in a research note.
WorldCom also said it still expected between $300 million and $350 million in cost reductions to result from its recently completed acquisition of MFS Communications, analysts said.
WorldCom acquired MFS Communications Co last December in a $12.6 billion stock swap.

Kastan said Internet-related revenue growth should continue to be the company's strongest line of business for the foreseeable future, driven by UUNET's extensive local infrastructure and an intense focus on the business market.
The company acquired UUNET as part of MFS Communications.
"WorldCom management spent more time than usual discussing the Internet and international (business), which are the company's fastest growing businesses right now," Meltzer said.
International opportunities should boost growth the next few years, especially WorldComs focus on Europe, Kastan said.

"With local networks in place and a pan-European long haul network in the works, WorldCom should prove quite nimble and able to successfully 'cherry pick' profitable telecom opportunities," Kastan said.
